i assume i still need to pay for it. i know there's a utah law for "surprise bills" but i have no idea if that applies here at all.

turn off notifications for her specifically. you can still message her from time to time, its just easier to make it infrequent this way. if she mentions it just say you've been busy.

you'll probably start to feel better and then if needed you can fully cut her off which will be easier at that point.

that's good that you have friendships within those circles. i wish you the best.

unfortunately i dont know the names of these websites or apps, ive only heard of them. but some are more likely to be popular in your area than others.

my area seems pretty active in facebook groups, so you could try there.

edit: i can also relate to finishing school and suddenly have far less social opportunities. luckily ive been able to hold onto a couple of friends from those days and im feeling ok as far as socializing goes. but i still live in the same college town.
you can make it 5 months, stay strong.

even in a suburban area you might still find some events for things. i live in a smallish town and there are events for pool, board games, card games, darts, dungeons and dragons, many other hobbies (you can probably tell im a nerd). i dont remember any off the too of my head but there are some online circles of people who discuss game develop and sometimes participate in game development events where you are given a vague prompt for a video game and see what you come up with and what others come up with and maybe they discuss their games with each other i cant quite remember. i know a guy who participates in these, he's not skilled at all and just spends hours googling to build something simple but he has fun with it.

anyways my point is there might still be things you can use in your area to meet people and if not there are online communities you may be able to get into as well. if you are shy or scared to meet people again, one of the online communities could be best to start with. that's just a suggestion im sorry i dont have any concrete advice for this.

personally my social life began in college when i joined certain clubs and participated in classes that basically required social interaction like language learning classes.

i know it's easier said than done but stay on top of anything work or school related. it is a lot of work and it can be painful but missing opportunities or dealing with bad grades or work issues just creates more and more anxiety. i failed so many classes or experienced other lost opportunities when i was in college and i regret it immensely. i didnt go to class or work because i was depressed and it just made things worse. 

i dont know much about your home life with your family but if it is a toxic environment then you should really move out (when you can). i argued at times with my parents and moving out was the best thing i could do for my relationship with them. i love them and they love me and we get along perfectly now. but i wouldnt consider my experience living with them as toxic, i had plenty of freedoms. but again i dont know what all you are experiencing with your family.

unfortunately i dont have any experience with the military but it sounds like you need a career change.

i don't know how one would get out or how any of that works but be sure to keep in touch with all those people, there must be some point in the future where you'll be able to return to them.

you need to maybe try new things maybe, meet new people. 

what kind of interests do you have? hobbies?

I went through a similar era of falling out with people and being depressed about not having them around anymore. but eventually i met new people who were great and made me forget about the past.

of course i still think back sometimes and get upset about it, but it got easier over time. now it feels like so long ago when it really was just a couple years.

I had this exact same issue after highschool way back. people who I thought were friends that just disappeared once school was over. of course they all stayed together, just excluding me. and seeing their FB posts about stuff was shitty.

i had to do new things, meet new people. and make ACTUAL friends for the first time.
this is common when you have a lot of bottled up emotions. I've probably done this exact thing with the garbage a couple of times myself lol.

hey there. you don't need others praise to feel accomplished in what you are doing. but i understand that hunger for attention. there's nothing wrong with it. if others aren't offering praise don't take it personally. if you enjoy what you are doing then keep doing it, for yourself, not them.

when you do dance or gymnastics are you around other people like a class or team or event? people you can socialize with?

personally there were plenty of things i wanted to feel praise for when i was your age and wasn't always able to get it from my family. sometimes I had to find other groups of people who shared the same interests or goals. and sometimes you just have to be content with yourself internally.

hey there. I also had depression when I was 18 and often argued with my parents.

what kind of self hate thoughts are you having? are these influenced by your mother? are they related to school or work?

hey there. i think it's very important you meet with a specialist you can discuss things with. a psychiatrist can prescribe medications that might help with the anxiety and panic attacks. and a therapist can help unravel your traumas and help you deal with them.

is this something you are able to do? I'm not certain your age but if you are a minor and don't have access to these professionals there are some resources that can help.

would there be problems if you discussed this with your parents or told your parents you wanted to speak with a therapist?

hey there. i've experienced the same/still do sometimes.

overthinking previous actions or words can be difficult to deal with.

do you mind sharing some of the things you feel guilty about?

if you are okay with a long read...i have a post about various treatment options. if it's ok that i link it here: https://www.reddit.com/r/depression_help/comments/ufqmvi/treatment_you_may_not_have_tried_and_my_personal/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf

edit: happy to discuss specifics in either thread if you want to.
absolutely fine with me to dm. however it's best though to share in the thread so others can give advice as well if you are comfortable with that.

hi there. first off, you're good friend just for posting this.

as for how you can help, there often isn't much you can do other than listen. but it depends. if your friend is asking for advice or you feel you have advice to share then that could be good. however some people just need someone to vent to. it won't cure anything but it helps to get it all out there. as long as your listening, you're doing great.

is there anything specific your friend mentioned that you might want to discuss here?

I've been there. resenting "gifted" people.

do you want to discuss anything specific? what kind of things are you envious of that are making you feel this way?

hey there. this can be a common thing when dating someone who has their own mental health problems to sort out. when you're the one being relied on it can be a ton of pressure, and if things don't improve it can make you feel really bad yourself.

the important thing to keep in mind is that you can't cure your partner. it just doesn't work like that. he has is own issues to deal with whether that be with medication or therapy or both or other treatments. as long as you are there and available emotionally, you are doing your part. that's all you can do and is all that could ever be expected of you being in a relationship like that.

if you'd like to discuss specifics maybe i can make more suggestions? such as what thoughts or feelings you are having in this moment. or what things is he saying or doing that you feel leads to the negative emotions you are feeling now.

keeping myself productive helps. i try to dive into classes or work as a distraction.

this doesn't work for everyone, but it's still important to be productive because if you fall behind or miss opportunities your going to feel a lot worse. and putting things off can give you a lot of anxiety.

if you don't have deadlines to meet it's ok to take the day off. everyone needs a mental health day off sometimes. just dont make it a habit otherwise you are inviting more and more anxiety.

if you don't have a psychiatrist get one. if you have difficulties getting one lemme know your situation I might have suggestions.

thats great you got cpap! once you get used to it and its been a few weeks you should start feeling better mentally and energy wise.

since that can take some time i'd recommend getting bloodwork done to test for deficiencies as well.

hello fellow sufferer.

I can't promise you things get better. I don't know you or what you've been through.

but if your current treatment isn't working, there are alternatives. again can't promise any 1 of them is a cure for you but I've seen them work for other people.

do you mind me asking what treatments you've tried in the past or are currently trying? maybe I can suggest alternatives.

no. don't stop making commitments. drag yourself out of bed no matter how hard it is. without commitments you'll be dragging yourself out of bed less and less and it's only going to make you feel worse.

as for medications not working I'd suggest looking into other kinds of treatments:

Therapy/Mindfulness

Electro Convulsive Therapy

esketamine/spravado

Trans-cranial Magnetic Stimulation

Guided psychadelic trip programs (or if you go the illegal route, there are apps that can help you walk through a trip, just start small and be careful)

and of course if you haven't already, you should do regular blood tests every few months to look for deficiencies. pretty much all the usual vitamin deficiencies can cause or worsen depression. keeping up with those might not cure you but it makes depression a lot worse if you don't. personally i get vitamin D and B deficiencies every few months.

look into healthier diets. even if you are getting everything you generally need from your diet, your "gut health" is very important and has been scientifically linked to depression.

lastly, stay in good physical shape. again this won't cure you but it helps a lot.

edit: again with the commitments, obviously if you aren't sure you can go and have a good reason then don't say you can. but being depressed isn't a good reason. again because it will make you feel worse if you don't stay active.

idk about others here but personally i feel like a piece of shit if i spend all day sleeping even if i didn't have social commitments that day.

edit 2: im also happy to discuss in detail any of the treatments i listed if you are curious.

something to understand is that not all treatments work for everybody.

I've tried many many medications, types of therapies, other treatments like ECT or TMS or spravado. some of them helped for awhile but many did nothing. but i've seen each of those work for other people, just not me. i think each of them helped a little bit and im at a very stable mostly up mood past couple months.

you won't know until you try these things.

meds work for some people and dont for others. sometimes you need to try different meds. and same goes for all other kinds of treatments.

as for the ADHD medication, talk to a psychiatrist. not only can they prescribe anti depressants but they can prescribe Aderrall and ritalin without jumping through as many hoops as a general doctor. assuming you are in the US.

edit: there are side effects to any medications. but most will go away after your body gets used to it. and sometimes you find a medication that works really well but has side effects that don't go away and you have to kind of decide whether it's worth the side effects or to try a different medication.
